comparisons.peer_summary: Card income increased $230 million primarily due to higher late fees, annual fees and card transfer fees.
comparisons.comparison: Both JPMorgan and Bank of America reported increases in Card Income for 2024, but they attributed these increases to different primary drivers. JPMorgan cited higher net interchange on increased sales volume and higher annual fees in its Consumer & Community Banking (CCB) segment, partially offset by amortization of origination costs. In contrast, Bank of America attributed its $230 million increase primarily to higher late fees, annual fees, and card transfer fees, without mentioning interchange or volume growth as the primary drivers.

comparisons.peer_summary: Revenues increased 6%, driven by a 5% rise in net interest income from strong loan growth and a 24% increase in non-interest revenue, which was largely due to lower partner payments and higher interchange fees, partially offset by increased rewards costs.
comparisons.comparison: Both JPMorgan and Citigroup discussed the impact of rewards costs and partner payments on card income, though in opposite directions. JPMorgan noted that higher net interchange from increased sales volume was partially offset by an increase in amortization related to new account origination costs. Citigroup reported that its increase in non-interest revenue (including interchange fees from higher card spend volume) was partially offset by an increase in rewards costs. Additionally, Citigroup explicitly cited lower partner payments as a driver, whereas JPMorgan did not mention partner payments.

sentences.text: Card income increased, reflecting higher net interchange on increased debit and credit card sales volume, as well as higher annual fees in CCB, partially offset by an increase in amortization related to new account origination costs.

The increase in non-interest revenue was largely driven by lower partner payments in Retail Services, due to higher net credit losses, and an increase in interchange fees (see Note 5), driven by higher card spend volume in Branded Cards.
The increase in non-interest revenue was partially offset by an increase in rewards costs in Branded Cards, driven by the higher card spend volume.
